map.Lessons 8-4, 8-5 & 8-6 — part of the The: Lessons 8-4, 8-5 & 8-6 are part of the arc The Balance Vault. write & graph inequalities · solution sets · 6.AT.C.9. Read from start to end. Each gate gives hints and a worked example. It never blocks the page.
map.Episode 3. Same crew, same city — one fo: Episode 3. Same crew, same city. One part of the case. Turn the page when you're ready.
map.A freight lift waits at the shaft. A bra: A freight lift waits at the shaft. A brass plate shows the rule. The fog does not agree.
map.\"At least 12\" isn't one number. Twelve: "At least 12" is not just one number. Twelve works. Thirteen works. Fifty works. How do we write that?
map.With an inequality — a statement compari: With an inequality. It compares values. It can be true for MANY values at once.
map.Ada's manual graphs one: \"at most 20 de: Ada's manual graphs one. "At most 20 degrees" is t ≤ 20. Draw a FILLED circle on 20 and a ray toward the smaller numbers. Filled means 20 counts too.
map.The brass plate says the lift runs with: The brass plate says the lift runs with at least 12 crates of ballast. First, write the rule as an inequality. Let x = crates loaded. Then choose its number-line graph.
map.Conceptual: 'at least 12' means exactly: Conceptual: 'at least 12' means 12 is allowed AND anything bigger is allowed. Does your symbol include 12 itself?
map.Procedural: an included boundary gets a: Procedural: an included boundary gets a FILLED (closed) circle. The ray points to all the other values that keep the rule true. For 'at least', that means the bigger numbers.
map.All the true values together form the so: All the true values together are the solution set. This one is strictly less than. The boundary is not in it.
map.Like loot filters. t < 4 keeps 2 and 3.5: Like loot filters. t < 4 keeps 2 and 3.5. It rejects 4, because 4 < 4 is false.
map.Vent rule: v < 9. Tap EVERY card whose v: Vent rule: v < 9. Tap EVERY card whose value makes the rule true. Those vents open. Tap a false one and the fog gets thicker.
map.Conceptual: v < 9 is STRICT — a value jo: Conceptual: v < 9 is STRICT. A value is in the solution set only if it is really smaller than 9. The boundary fails its own rule: 9 < 9 is false.
map.Procedural: test the cards one at a time: Procedural: test the cards one at a time, decimals too. Practice with t < 4: 2 opens a vent because 2 < 4 is true. 4.2 stays sealed because 4.2 < 4 is false.
map.Balance is not stillness. It is truth, h: Balance is not standing still. It is truth, held steady. Prove three truths and we can breathe.
map.Locks 1 and 2 are one-step equations. Lo: Locks 1 and 2 are one-step equations. Lock 3 is the gauge. The door stays open only while p ≤ 15 is true.
map.Reader — you've leveled beams and read s: Reader, you've leveled beams and read symbols all night. Now call the truths!
map.Boss Gate: inverse operations on both si: Boss Gate: use inverse operations on both sides. Then test the pressure set. Remember what ≤ includes.
map.Ada's vault door. Lock 1: m − 6 = 9. Loc: Ada's vault door. Lock 1: m − 6 = 9. Lock 2: 4t = 36. Lock 3: the door stays open only while the pressure keeps p ≤ 15 true. Choose the set of readings that never breaks the rule.
map.Conceptual: each lock did ONE thing to i: Conceptual: each lock did ONE thing to its variable. Undo it with the inverse, on BOTH sides. And ≤ means 'less than OR EQUAL'. The boundary keeps the rule true.
map.Procedural: Lock 1: undo − 6 by ADDING 6: Procedural: Lock 1: undo − 6 by ADDING 6 to both sides. Lock 2: undo × 4 by DIVIDING both sides by 4. Lock 3: test EVERY number in a set against the gauge. One false reading shuts the door again.
map.The fog's venting — every grate at once!: The fog is clearing from every grate at once! TRUE statements, five for five!
map.And inside: Ada's eighth journal… plus t: And inside: Ada's eighth journal and the city account book she balanced by hand.

map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.x > 12 leaves 12 itself OUT — but the pl: x > 12 leaves 12 OUT. But the plate says exactly 12 crates is enough to run.
map.x ≤ 12 points the wrong way: 'at least': x ≤ 12 points the wrong way. 'At least' allows MORE ballast, not less.
map.x = 12 allows only exactly 12 — but 13 c: x = 12 allows only 12. But 13 crates or 50 crates also work for 'at least 12.'
map.An OPEN circle means 12 is NOT included: An OPEN circle means 12 is NOT included. But the lift runs with exactly 12. Look for a filled circle.
map.That ray slides toward values SMALLER th: That ray goes toward values SMALLER than 12. The lift needs 12 or MORE.
map.A single point shows only x = 12. The ru: A single point shows only x = 12. The rule is true for many values. Where is the ray?
map.x ≥ 12: closed circle at 12, ray to the: x ≥ 12: closed circle at 12, ray to the right. The lift hums awake and takes the crew down.
map.9 < 9 is false — the boundary stays seal: 9 < 9 is false, so the boundary stays sealed. A strict < never lets its own boundary in.
map.12 < 9 is false — that card feeds the fo: 12 < 9 is false, so that card feeds the fog. Only values SMALLER than 9 clear it.
map.True values are still fogged in. EVERY c: Some true values are still in the fog. EVERY card smaller than 9 is in the solution set, decimals too.
map.Lock 1 holds. 9 − 6 undoes the WRONG way: Lock 1 stays shut. 9 − 6 goes the WRONG way. m had 6 taken AWAY, so give 6 back. Add 6 to both sides.
map.Lock 1 holds. Undo − 6 with its inverse:: Lock 1 stays shut. Undo − 6 with its inverse: add 6 to BOTH sides.
map.Lock 2 holds. You multiplied — but 4t me: Lock 2 stays shut. You multiplied, but 4t already means 4 × t. Undo × 4 by dividing both sides by 4.
map.Lock 2 holds. 4t means 4 × t. Apply the: Lock 2 stays shut. 4t means 4 × t. Use the inverse of multiplication on both sides.
map.Lock 3 holds. 15 ≤ 15 is true… but 16 ≤: Lock 3 stays shut. 15 ≤ 15 is true… but 16 ≤ 15 is FALSE. One bad reading seals the door again.
map.Lock 3 holds. 16 ≤ 15 is false and 20 ≤: Lock 3 stays shut. 16 ≤ 15 is false and 20 ≤ 15 is false. That set slams the door twice.
map.Lock 3 holds. 0 ≤ 15 is true, but 22 ≤ 1: Lock 3 stays shut. 0 ≤ 15 is true, but 22 ≤ 15 is false. EVERY reading must keep the rule true.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. m = 15, t = 9, and {12,: ALL LOCKS OPEN. m = 15, t = 9, and {12, 15} keeps p ≤ 15 true. 15 ≤ 15 counts! The fog rises and clears. The Balance Vault gives in.
